# Temple Scroll Column 58 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

This log records all lines in Temple Scroll Column 58 where the three translators significantly diverged, along with SOPHIA's resolution.

---

## 58:3 — "plotting evil" vs. "devising evil" vs. "planning to attack"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "plotting evil against his people" | Standard rendering of choshev ra'ah |
| LOGOS | "devising evil against his people" | Formal English synonym preserving the deliberative aspect |
| PNEUMA | "planning to attack his people" | Modern military language specifying the threat |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "devising evil" (LOGOS). "Plotting" (EMET) and "devising" are near-synonyms; LOGOS slightly more formal. PNEUMA's "planning to attack" narrows the scope — the Hebrew could include non-military threats.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 58:8 — "fearful-hearted" vs. "fainthearted" vs. "fearful"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "fearful-hearted" | Literal rakh ha-levav — "soft of heart" |
| LOGOS | "fainthearted" | Standard English equivalent |
| PNEUMA | "fearful" | Simplified modern adjective |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "fainthearted" (LOGOS). The traditional Deuteronomic term for those exempt from military service; PNEUMA's "fearful" loses the compositional quality.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 58:12 — "fear of the LORD" vs. "dread of the LORD" vs. "terror of the LORD"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "fear of the LORD" | Standard yir'at YHWH |
| LOGOS | "dread of the LORD" | Distinguished from reverential fear — this is the panic that falls on enemies |
| PNEUMA | "terror of the LORD" | Strongest rendering, emphasizing the military context |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "dread" (LOGOS). In military contexts, the divine fear that falls on enemy nations is more than reverence — "dread" captures this without PNEUMA's excess.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 58:18 — "acts treacherously" vs. "acts unfaithfully" vs. "violates"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "acts treacherously against the Torah" | Strong rendering of ma'al — covenant betrayal |
| LOGOS | "acts unfaithfully against the Torah" | Standard covenantal vocabulary — ma'al denotes breach of faith |
| PNEUMA | "violates the Torah" | Direct modern legal language |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "acts unfaithfully" (LOGOS). Ma'al has a specific covenantal dimension — it denotes breach of faith/trust, not mere violation. "Treacherously" (EMET) is too strong; "violates" (PNEUMA) loses the relational dimension.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 58:20 — "by his own authority" vs. "on his own authority" vs. scope of limitation

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "by his own authority" | Literal — the king acts solo |
| LOGOS | "on his own authority" | Same concept, standard English preposition |
| PNEUMA | "on his own authority; only the council may authorize capital punishment" | Expanded explanation of the restriction |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS phrasing. PNEUMA's expansion, while clarifying, adds interpretive language not in the source. The Hebrew is concise and the translation should match.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 58:21 — hierarchy clause — constitutional significance

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "shall be subject to the Torah and to the council" | Clear subordination language |
| LOGOS | "shall be subject to the Torah and to the council" | Same |
| PNEUMA | "is answerable to the Torah and to the council" | Modern accountability language |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "subject to" (EMET/LOGOS). Both renderings are valid; "subject to" has a more constitutional ring appropriate for this foundational governance clause.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/LOGOS.

---
